Action Plan:
1. Suspected acute decompensation of chronic heart failure – increase Furosemide from 1 tablet daily to 1 tablet twice daily for the next few days; monitor symptom response.  
2. Order same-day blood tests (full blood count, renal function/electrolytes) to assess for anaemia and monitor kidney status while on higher-dose diuretic.  
3. Arrange outpatient transthoracic echocardiogram within 1–2 weeks to reassess left-ventricular function.  
4. Schedule follow-up review (telehealth or in-person) in 1 week to evaluate breathlessness, ankle swelling, and review test results.  
5. Safety-netting: patient to seek urgent care or call clinic sooner for worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or other new concerns.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Increasing shortness of breath over ~2 weeks, markedly worse in last few days; now breathless on minimal exertion (e.g., walking inside house).  
• Associated symptoms: Mild dry cough; bilateral ankle swelling noticed over past few days; denies chest pain, palpitations, fever, or appetite change.  
• Past medical history: Chronic heart failure; prior “small heart attack” (~5 years ago, likely myocardial infarction). No other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications:  
  – Furosemide (dose/frequency not documented; currently 1 tablet daily)  
  – Aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  – Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father died of heart attack in early 60s; mother alive with osteoporosis.  
• Social history: Lives alone with two cats; part-time lorry driver (day shifts); ex-smoker (≈1 pack/day for 25 years, now quit); no alcohol; walks to shops daily for exercise.

Objective:
• General: Doctor states chest examination, oxygen saturation, and blood pressure “all OK”; no numeric values provided.  
• Peripheral oedema: Bilateral ankle swelling reported; no physical description documented.  
• No additional physical findings or vitals recorded in transcript.  
• Investigations today: None performed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Worsening breathlessness / oedema – likely acute decompensated chronic heart failure  
   – Assessment: Congestive heart failure exacerbation.  
   – Differential: Lower-respiratory infection, pulmonary embolism, anaemia (less likely given clinical picture).  
   – Investigations planned: CBC, renal function/electrolytes; transthoracic echocardiogram.  
   – Treatment planned: Increase Furosemide to 1 tablet twice daily for few days; monitor symptoms.  
   – Follow-up: Review in 1 week; earlier if deterioration.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Exact vital signs; physical examination details (lung auscultation, heart sounds, JVP); current doses/strengths of all medications; weight for diuretic titration; allergy review beyond drugs (e.g., environmental).  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Occasional audio dropouts (“connection not very good”) but clinically relevant information intelligible.
